title: Polarized Thomson scattering makes tested thin screens too bright for the ASASSN-14ko soft X-ray dip
abstract: We test whether a fully ionized screen can hide a steady soft X-ray source in ASASSN-14ko. We set the angular size of a uniform shell sector from the published ingress scale and faint-state span under circular motion. We follow polarized coherent Thomson scattering through all orders. For outer-to-inner radius ratios 1.01 and 1.1 and radial depths 8, 20 and 32, the scattered fraction is 0.0071-0.0325, above the published fixed-shape soft-component limit of 0.000421. Direct-beam attenuation alone would miss this failure. Radially extended sectors give smaller on-axis flux; a finite Gaussian source can change that flux substantially. The test limits these specified elastic screens. It does not exclude all occultation or establish intrinsic shutdown. Source geometry, steady illumination, the inherited spectral limit and coherent scattering are assumptions. Recoil, absorption, ionization and a moving-screen light curve are outside the test. We provide original transfer code, photon-conservation and ray tests, finite-source checks, aggregate results and input hashes. No new telescope measurement or orbital clock is claimed.

display.caption: Polarized coherent-scattering shell sectors. Point-source flux and scattered flux relative to the published soft limit. Error bars are two Monte Carlo standard errors. The curves are model scenarios, not confidence limits on gas geometry.
